thread:
inc-bot: ALERT: High error rate detected for app-gateway in us-central-2 — 5xx spike and proxy timeouts. 5m window: 11.8% 5xx, p95 latency 6.2s. Paging oncall. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/shot/INC-3187654321 :rotating_light:
Marta (oncall): Ack — I'm on it. Spinning up adhoc triage. Who's on network/edge?
Raj: I'm here, checking edge pool metrics now. Quick checks: CPU OK, but connection reuse is down. Running `ss -tnp | grep 443 | wc -l` shows many TIME_WAITs, and `edgeproxy` pods show high conn counts.
Olivia: linking routing config: route table shows us-central-2 weight 1.0 on prod. I can push a temporary reroute to us-east.
Lee: I'm seeing elevated redis timeouts from the region (reply latency ~1.2s -> 2.4s). Upstream cache failures causing errors to escalate. Not a pure compute OOM.
Marta (oncall): Customer impact? Jun, can you surface any high-severity customer reports?
Jun: CS queue shows 6 priority tickets in the last 8m referencing 'service errors' & 'requests failing intermittently' — some paying customers degraded. Draft comms ready once we have mitigation plan.
Raj: Running probe to confirm TLS handshake storm. `ss -s` shows many orphaned sockets. I suspect a client-side keepalive regression combined with heavier short requests.
Amy: On the runtime side, we're seeing KV cache TTL eviction spikes correlated with the error window. A config rollout earlier today bumped TTLs down for a test group; rolling that back might help.
Marta (oncall): Ok plan: 1) Shift traffic 60% to us-east failover pool. 2) Drain 2 hot pods in us-central-2 for a soft reset. 3) Rollback TTL change for cache testgroup. 4) Rate-limit unknown IPs above threshold. Execute in that order and report.
Olivia: I'll do the traffic steer. Command I'm running: ``rctl route update --from region:us-central-2 --to region:us-east-1 --weight 0.6 --reason "mitigation: 5xx spike"`` Will post confirmation when complete.
SRE-tilt-bot: routing-change: executed by olivia at 2026-03-15T18:07:50Z — weight updated, gradual shift in progress. :robot_face:
Lee: Starting node cordon+drain for the two highest-conn pods. Commands: ```kubectl cordon edge-node-usc2-07 && kubectl drain edge-node-usc2-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30``` Doing one at a time.
Raj: Also bumping TCP TIME_WAIT reuse to reduce socket churn on the proxies (temporary): `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse=1` applying to affected nodes via runbook. Will monitor for side effects.
Amy: Rolling back TTL change for testgroup: `kv-config set --group testgroup --kv.ttl=60s --target prod-usc2` -> revert to 300s. Applying now.
Marta (oncall): Good. Jun please prepare customer comms: short note acknowledging degraded service, mitigation steps, ETA 30m. I'll sign.
Jun: Draft: "We're aware of increased errors in US-Central affecting some requests. We've routed traffic to backup region and are actively mitigating. We'll update in 30m." Ready to send after Marta ack.
Olivia: Routing shift in-progress. Current traffic split (approx): us-central-2 40% / us-east-1 60%. Watching latency panels.
SRE-tilt-bot: metric-update: 5xx dropped from 11.8% -> 6.9% after initial 4m of reroute. p95 down to 4.1s.
Raj: After drain, the first pod restart cleared many TIME_WAITs. Conn reuse improved, TLS handshake retries reduced by ~40%.
Lee: Redis errors decreased after rollback, but a couple of replica syncs caught up — no data loss expected.
Marta (oncall): Good progress. Next: if rates <3% and p95 <2.5s for 10m, we'll keep the partial failover and start slowly shifting traffic back. If not, we escalate to full failover.
Olivia: Noted. I'm pausing additional routing moves until we see stable metrics.
Amy: Found a secondary thing — our circuit-breaker threshold for backend B was at 50 req/s; due to traffic churn it tripped briefly causing 502s. I've raised it to 120 req/s temporarily. Command: `cb-config set backend-b --threshold 120`
Raj: After that change and drains, the 502 fanout stopped. 5xx is now ~2.3% and p95 at 2.0s; still watching.
SRE-tilt-bot: metric-update: 5xx stabilized at 2.1% over last 6m. Incident severity downgraded to partial-degradation.
Jun: Preparing customer update v1: "Mitigation in progress; majority of traffic routed to backup region; errors substantially reduced; continuing to monitor; next update in 30 minutes."
Marta (oncall): Copy. I'll send once we confirm stability for 10m. I've also opened a post-incident ticket for root cause (tags: network-sockets, cache-ttl, circuit-breaker) and assigned owners: Raj, Lee, Amy.
Olivia: Quick note for runbook: consider adding a gradual TTL rollback and a preflight check for client keepalive regressions before TTL changes.
Raj: Follow-up immediate actions: capture netstat dumps, save proxy logs for the hour before spike, and export `ss` output. Command I used: ```ss -tnp state TIME-WAIT | awk '{print $5}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -n```
Marta (oncall): Thanks team. Status: mitigation in progress -> partial mitigation achieved. We'll keep the thread open for 60m and then update incident channel with final status.
Jun: Sent customer comms draft to CS distribution list.
SRE-tilt-bot: incident-note: mitigation-step completed by marta at 2026-03-15T18:20:00Z — traffic shift + drains + rollbacks applied.
Marta (oncall): Final update for now: 5xx down to 2.1% (was 11.8%). p95 latency 2.0s. Marking as 'monitoring' — will do full postmortem. Owners: Raj (net), Lee (cache), Amy (runtime). I'll create the followup doc in #postmortems with links to logs and the runbook changes. :thumbsup:
Raj: grabbing logs and uploading to S3 now. Path: s3://redwood-incident-logs/3187654321/
Lee: I'll validate redis replicas and add an action item to revert TTL test gating in the config pipeline.
Amy: I'll open a PR to change CB default thresholds and add canary checks for TTL rollouts.
Marta (oncall): Closing the paging rotation — thanks everyone. If any regressions spike again, re-open and we'll escalate.
SRE-tilt-bot: incident-archived: thread set to 'monitor-only' at 2026-03-15T18:29:25Z
